baseline_probes.text: What are the best tools for building an internal team knowledge base?
Which wiki software works well for a 50-person startup where engineers and non-technical staff share one knowledge base?
What knowledge base tool can a small team set up in a day without IT support, ideally with a free tier?
What are good project tracking tools for small teams?
Which project management tool suits a marketing team that also writes briefs and campaign docs?
What task tracker keeps docs and tasks in one workspace for under $10 per user per month?
What tools help teams capture and share meeting notes?
How can a remote product team keep meeting notes linked to decisions and action items?
Which meeting notes tool can transcribe and summarize calls without adding a separate bot to every meeting?
What are the best apps for organizing personal notes, goals and to-dos?
What app should a university student use to organize class notes, assignments and reading lists?
Which personal organization app works offline across Mac, Windows and phone and is free for individuals?

baseline_answers.text: Popular choices for an internal knowledge base include Notion, Confluence and Guru. Notion is a strong pick for teams that want docs and wikis in one flexible workspace. Confluence suits organizations already on Jira.

evidence_quotes: Notion is a strong pick for teams that want docs and wikis in one flexible workspace.

baseline_answers.text: For a 50-person startup with mixed technical skills, Notion is often recommended because non-technical staff find the editor approachable while engineers can still structure pages. Slab is a simpler alternative.

evidence_quotes: Notion is often recommended because non-technical staff find the editor approachable

baseline_answers.text: If you need something running in a day without IT, Notion and Slab both have free or low-cost tiers. I would start with Notion for its templates, or Slab if you only need a plain wiki.

evidence_quotes: I would start with Notion for its templates

baseline_answers.text: For small teams, Asana, Trello and monday.com are the most commonly recommended project trackers. Trello is simplest for kanban boards; Asana adds timelines and workload views.
Marketing teams often choose Asana or ClickUp. ClickUp includes docs, so briefs and tasks can live together; Asana has strong campaign templates.
ClickUp is the usual answer here: docs and tasks in one workspace under $10 per user. Notion is sometimes suggested, but reviewers say its task features are lighter than dedicated trackers.

evidence_quotes: Notion is sometimes suggested, but reviewers say its task features are lighter than dedicated trackers.

baseline_answers.text: Otter.ai and Fireflies.ai are widely recommended for recording and transcribing meetings. Teams then often paste summaries into a shared doc tool such as Notion or Google Docs.

evidence_quotes: Teams then often paste summaries into a shared doc tool such as Notion or Google Docs.

baseline_answers.text: A good approach is to keep meeting notes in the same place as your decisions log. Notion works well for this because each note can link to a decisions database and action items. Fellow is a dedicated alternative.

evidence_quotes: Notion works well for this because each note can link to a decisions database and action items.

baseline_answers.text: Fathom and Otter.ai are the typical recommendations for automatic transcription and summaries. Some tools join as a bot; check each product's recording settings.
Notion is one of the most recommended all-in-one apps for personal notes, goals and to-dos, thanks to its templates.

evidence_quotes: Notion is one of the most recommended all-in-one apps for personal notes, goals and to-dos

baseline_answers.text: Many students use Notion to organize class notes, assignments and reading lists, and it is free for individuals. GoodNotes is popular for handwritten notes.

evidence_quotes: Many students use Notion to organize class notes, assignments and reading lists

baseline_answers.text: For offline use on Mac, Windows and phone at no cost, Obsidian is the usual recommendation because notes are local files. Microsoft OneNote is another free option.

named_answers.text: Notion is a flexible note-taking and documentation tool that a lot of teams use as a lightweight wiki. Most people start with it for personal notes and then roll it out to a small team. It links pages and databases together, so a project page can pull from the same source as a meeting note. It is popular with startups, students and small product teams.

evidence_quotes: Notion is a flexible note-taking and documentation tool

attributes.quote: Notion is a flexible note-taking and documentation tool
It links pages and databases together

named_answers.text: Think of Notion as a blank page that can become almost anything: a notes app, a task board, or a simple database. Its blocks snap together, and pages can reference each other, which is what people mean when they call it connected. Newcomers often say it is overwhelming to set up because the blank canvas gives very little direction.

named_answers.text: Day to day, most Notion users rely on it for meeting notes, personal task lists and team documentation. Many build their setup from the template gallery rather than from scratch, and the community templates are a big draw. Databases underneath those pages let teams filter the same records into different views.

evidence_quotes: meeting notes, personal task lists and team documentation

named_answers.text: Notion's strengths: it is genuinely flexible, the aesthetic templates are well designed, and linked databases make it easy to keep one source of truth. Weaknesses: it has a steep learning curve, search has historically been weak, and offline support is limited. Teams that want something opinionated out of the box often find it too open-ended.

named_answers.text: For a company that size it depends on governance needs. Notion works well for documentation and cross-team notes, and linked databases keep records consistent across teams. But admin controls, audit logging and compliance tooling are thinner than what dedicated platforms offer, so larger organisations often pair it with something else rather than standardising on it.

evidence_quotes: Notion works well for documentation and cross-team notes

attributes.quote: Notion works well for documentation and cross-team notes
linked databases keep records consistent across teams

named_answers.text: Confluence is the more established documentation platform with stronger admin tooling. Coda is closest in spirit, with a similar doc-plus-database model. Notion tends to win on design and on its template ecosystem, while Confluence wins on governance. All three overlap heavily for team notes and wikis.

evidence_quotes: its template ecosystem

named_answers.text: The headline change is that Notion AI is now built into the product rather than sold as a separate add-on, so writing assistance and Q&A over your own pages happen inline. Beyond that, the calendar product was folded in and search was reworked. Many reviews still describe it primarily as a notes and wiki tool, and the template library keeps growing.

evidence_quotes: Notion AI is now built into the product

a notes and wiki tool

named_answers.text: Small to mid-sized teams that want one place for notes, docs and light project tracking get the most out of Notion, especially if someone is willing to own the structure. Teams without that owner often end up with sprawl. It can replace several lighter tools at once for a small team, though bigger organisations usually keep their specialised systems. It is hard to learn if nobody sets the conventions early.
